# Interactive Message Overview

**Source:** https://open.seatalk.io/docs/interactive-msg_overview

Interactive message cards are a flexible message type that can be used in various scenarios. The documents under this section will introduce what is an interactive message card, what it can do, where it can be used and lastly, some practical examples and sample codes that you can directly use to suit your own need. You can also refer to the detailed documents under each section to find out more. 

![D9QJTTEBZZFaAAAAAElFTkSuQmCC](data:image/png;base64,)

## What is Interactive Message

Interactive message cards are a powerful message type that conveys structured information to end-users with additional capabilities to support user interactions.

Now the Interactive Message supports 6 types of elements below, which can be combined as your needs freely.

| # | Element | Feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Title | A text element for leading the interactive message |
| 2 | Description | A text element for one or several pararaphs |
| 3 | Callback Button | An interactive button which allows the user to easily tap |
| 4 | Redirect Button | An interactive button which redirect the user to an app page or a website |
| 5 | Button Group | A component which can contain buttons, allowing them to be laid out in a single line |
| 6 | Image | An image element which helps recipients understand context at a glance with inline visuals |

*More element types will be supported in the future.

- Flexible: every interactive message card consists of different elements that can be customised. You can imagine an interactive message card as a lego that consists of different pieces. Each piece can be unique on its own

- Interactive: being interactive is a killer benefit of interactive message cards! Buttons (and different types of buttons) bring interactive message cards alive by enabling simple user interactions, which leads communication to the next level by making it more efficient

- Info-rich: compared to other message types such as plain texts, interactive message cards are much more info-rich since each card is a container of other message types. With a clear and structured card layout, interactive message cards deliver a more visually appealing user experience

Because of the powerful customisation of card elements, an interactive message card can be used in many scenarios to suit different needs. The versatility makes interactive message cards a common capability that is integrated with many communication channels (see "Use Interactive Message Cards in Your App" below for detail).

## What Can Interactive Messages Do

Interactive message cards provide many benefits:

- They make two-way interaction more convenient and efficient

- They provide an elegant and friendly user experience that is visually appealing

- They suit abundant usage scenarios:

- They can collect information from users by giving them some pre-defined options

- They can guide users to a further scenario by serving as an entry/redirection point

- They can present images directly in the card to enrich context

When you need to illicit user response/acknowledgement or to guide users into a further scenario, interactive message cards are an elegant solution that makes the workflow more efficient and joyful. Below are some typical examples where interactive message cards can be used:

- Approval-related scenarios: for example, a ticket approval app contains some approval logic that requires some app users to approve requests. It can send an interactive message card to a user asking for quick approval/rejection of a task ticket

- Notifications that invite users to visit your web/RN app: for example, an employee engagement forum app has a web/RN app touchpoint and wants to engage with employees outside the app when someone has commented on their post. It can send an interactive message card to a user informing them of the comment activity and inviting them to visit that particular post in the app

For more concrete examples and sample code, see Sample Code (/docs/interactive-msg_sample-code).

## Which Channel Supports Interactive Messages

As a common capability provided on SeaTalk Open Platform, interactive messages can be used in diverse communication channels to adapt to different usage scenarios.

| # | Sender | Channel | Supported? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | App | App Center | Yes |
| 2 | Bot | 1-on-1 Chat | Yes |
| 3 | Bot | Group Chat | Yes |
| 4 | System Account | Group Chat | Yes |

See Build a Card (/docs/interactive-msg_build-a-card) for a thorough introduction to the structure of an interactive message card, the card elements currently supported, how to build an interactive message card and the internationalisation of the card content.

After understanding how to build one interactive message card, it's time to let it do its magic. See Send a Card (/docs/interactive-msg_send-a-card) for a step-by-step introduction to configuring everything your app needs to send out a card, as well as the relative server APIs available.

Lastly, you can refer to Sample Code (/docs/interactive-msg_sample-code) for some inspiration on how to design a typical interactive message card.

## Update a Sent Interactive Message

An interactive message can be updated after sent:

- Bots can update interactive messages sent to their users

- Bots can update interactive messages sent to group chats

See Update Message (https://open.seatalk.io/docs/Update-Interactive-Message-Card) for API details.
